description: 10 Men is a large format menswear magazine from London, published twice a year to follow the men's collections. Each issue is organised around a trio of themed words and runs long fashion stories, cover interviews with actors and musicians, and conversations with designers, with several collectable covers per issue. It suits readers who follow luxury menswear and fashion photography closely.

10 Magazine is the womenswear title from the same London house as 10 Men, appearing twice a year in step with the collections. Issues carry long photographic stories built around individual luxury houses, interviews with designers, models and musicians, and a dozen or so alternative covers. It is for readers who want high fashion imagery in a thick, seasonal object.

a Dance Mag is a small format English language magazine about dance as it is lived around the world, from ritual and folk forms to club floors and contemporary stages. Each issue takes one theme and fills it with essays, reportage, interviews and a photographic poster insert. It is for dancers, scholars and anyone curious about movement as culture rather than as performance review.

Each issue of this Paris fashion title is handed to a single designer or house, who fills it with their own references, from photography and art to music, places and friends. The result reads as a portrait of a designer's mind rather than a season's coverage, and recent guests include Cecilie Bahnsen and Hiroshi Fujiwara. It is for readers interested in how designers think and for collectors of fashion publications.

Acid Magazine is a thick bilingual French and English annual that uses surfing as a way into the ocean itself, taking in oceanography, coastal economies, environmental questions, art, fashion and history. The latest number runs to 400 pages and fifteen stories in a compact format, issued with four different covers. It suits readers of surf and ocean culture who want essays and photography rather than contest results or gear.

Adbusters is the Vancouver bimonthly that has been attacking consumer culture since 1989, mixing political and philosophical essays with spoof advertisements, collage and hand lettered design in an almost ad free package. Recent issues take on AI driven culture and the state of liberal politics. It is read by activists, designers and students interested in media criticism and culture jamming.

Aleï Journal is a Paris photography and art publication that gives long portfolio runs to image makers with raw or unconventional practices and keeps text to a minimum. Each issue appears with several alternative covers by different photographers. It is for readers of contemporary fashion and art photography and for collectors of photo publications.

Antidote Magazine is a French fashion and culture title built on long interviews and black and white portrait series with musicians, writers and actors, many from the French rap and pop scene. Since 2026 each issue comes as a large 30 by 40 cm revue and a cheaper pocket fanzine with the same contents, each with several covers. It is for French speaking readers who follow music, fashion and youth culture and want a collectable object.

Applied Arts is a Canadian magazine for the visual communications trade, covering advertising, graphic design, photography and illustration. Its two issues a year are largely awards annuals presenting the winners of the magazine's own competitions alongside interviews and features on creative practice. It is bought by designers, art directors, photographers and marketing people, mainly in Canada.

description: Arc Poetry Magazine is Canada's poetry magazine, printing new poems, translations, reviews, interviews and close reading columns three times a year, with a featured artist on the cover and inside. Each issue also carries the results of one of its contests, such as the Poem of the Year. It is for poets, students and anyone following contemporary Canadian poetry.

Autre is a large format Los Angeles magazine on art, fashion and culture, with each issue built around one theme such as surveillance or wellness. Issues run several hundred pages of long interviews, essays and photography, carry four alternative covers and include a digital edition with every print order. It is for readers of contemporary art and culture criticism who want a theme driven, collectable object twice a year.

Backstage Talks is a magazine of long conversations with designers, studio founders and creative directors about the business behind the work, from pricing and growth to how decisions get made. The latest issue centres on complexity and change and adds a short crash course in complexity science. It suits working designers, studio owners and design students.

Badlon is a thick annual almanac of fashion photography, art and visual essays from France, each edition released with several covers by different young artists. The sixth issue runs to 510 pages of fashion stories, photography and texts around escapism, subcultures and imagined inner worlds. It is for collectors of fashion and photography books rather than readers after regular features.

Based Istanbul is a bilingual Turkish and English magazine about the city's creative scene, mixing fashion, art, architecture, design, film and music through interviews, portraits and photo stories. Each themed issue appears with several covers featuring Turkish actors and musicians alongside international names. It is for readers following Turkish fashion and popular culture and the people shaping it.

BASIC is a Beverly Hills fashion and art magazine built around themed issues, each released with two or three covers featuring actors, musicians and designers. Inside are fashion editorials, beauty and art stories, designer profiles and interviews across 128 pages in a coffee table format. It is for readers of glossy fashion photography and celebrity led style coverage.

BlackFlash is a contemporary art magazine from the Canadian prairies that grew out of photography and now covers photo, video, digital, performance and other image based practices. Each issue carries feature essays, artist profiles, conversations and commissioned artist projects, mostly on Canadian artists. It is for artists, curators, writers and students of contemporary art.

BLAG, or Better Letters Magazine, is an advertising free magazine entirely about sign painting, from hand lettered shopfronts and gilding to fairground and showcard lettering and the people who make them around the world. Each eighty page issue mixes technique guides, historical features, project profiles and a fold out poster. It is for working sign painters, lettering artists and anyone drawn to hand made commercial lettering.

Blanc is a quarterly fashion, art and music magazine built around cover stories with musicians and artists, long interviews and fashion editorials, printed at 315 by 230 mm. It gives space to voices the mainstream glossies tend to pass over. It is for readers of culture and fashion magazines who want a broader cast than the newsstand offers.

BRICKS is a British fashion and culture magazine with an activist streak, pairing cover interviews with musicians, models and public figures with fashion editorials and essays on social issues. Each themed issue appears roughly once a year with multiple covers alongside a running online edition. It suits readers of youth culture fashion titles who want politics and community woven in.

British Journal of Photography is the long running London photography magazine, now printed quarterly, with each issue built around a theme such as maps, the body or the annual Ones to Watch selection of emerging photographers. Issues combine portfolios, interviews and critical essays on documentary, fine art and commissioned photography from around the world. It is read by working photographers, picture editors, students and collectors who follow contemporary photography.
